public_rationale: Primary studies published before the post document repeated reproduction of training material. The GPT-2 study includes a 1,450-line code file and complete license texts. The later study finds many distinct verbatim sequences across several models. These results support the ordinary meaning of lengthy, repeated memorization without requiring a particular numerical threshold.
limitations: Extraction methods can involve deliberate prompting and specialized decoding.
The evidence does not establish how often ordinary users encounter lengthy reproductions.
It does not establish a universal training-data threshold or show that all training material is memorized.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Given enough data, LLMs have demonstrably duplicated lengthy training materials multiple times (memorization).

statement.excerpt: LLMs don’t store things in simple databases, but when presented with enough data, their regeneration of distributed bits has demonstrably duplicated lengthy training materials multiple times, a phenomenon that is called memorization in the field.

from_speaker: LLMs don’t store things in simple databases
has demonstrably duplicated lengthy training materials multiple times
our_interpretation: This asserts that repeated examples of substantial training-text reproduction had been demonstrated by the post date.
Lengthy means extended passages or substantial code, rather than common short phrases. Multiple times means more than one demonstrated reproduction, not a minimum frequency in ordinary use.
Enough data describes the training setting. It does not specify a universal data-volume threshold or assert that every model reproduces every passage.
The wording has demonstrably duplicated refers to accumulated past demonstrations, so the target period has no stated beginning and ends on the post date.
The database distinction concerns text generated by learned model parameters, rather than text fetched through an external retrieval system.
criteria.support_condition: Primary research documents multiple extended outputs matching training material from neural language models, with methods that distinguish memorization from retrieval or accidental phrase overlap.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant demonstrations are invalidated, or their apparent reproductions are shown to be prompt copying, external retrieval, or coincidental short overlap rather than generation of memorized training passages.

evidence.explanation: The GPT-2 study documents an entire code file and complete license texts among its extended extractions. These are multiple substantial reproductions, well beyond ordinary short-phrase overlap.

The study matches generated outputs against the open models' training datasets, requiring verbatim sequences of at least 50 tokens. It reports hundreds of thousands to millions of distinct matching sequences, independently supporting repeated memorization.
